parole.significato: bentgrass, couch grass (any of numerous reedy grass species of the genus Agrostis)
parole.testo: From French agrostis, from Ancient Greek ἄγρωστις (ágrōstis).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἄδεια (ádeia), with semantic loan from French permission, permis, licence.

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἄκαμπτος. Morphologically, from ά- (á-, privative α-) + κάμπτω καμπτ- (kámpto kampt-, “bend, turn around”) + -ος (-os). The figurative sense, semantic loan from French inflexible.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἄκανθα f (ákantha). Sense for architecture, semantic loan from French acanthe < Latin acanthus from Ancient Greek ἄκανθος m (ákanthos) for which also see άκανθος m (ákanthos). Also see αγκάθι n (agkáthi, “thorn”).

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἄνθραξ (ánthrax, “charcoal”), from the accusative singular "τόν (tón) ἄνθρακα (ánthraka); compare dialectal άθρακας (áthrakas, “disease, pestilence”). For the chemical sense, semantic loan from French carbone. For the disease, semantic loan from English anthrax,

parole.significato: are, a unit of area equal to ¹⁄₁₀₀ hectare or 100 square metres
parole.testo: from French are

Inherited from Ancient Greek ἄστρον (ástron). The figurative sense of "fate" since Mediaeval times. The contemporary terms of the emblem or geometrical shape, semantic loan from French étoile. For "Star Wars", semantic loan from English Star Wars
From Ancient Greek ἄτομον (átomon), neuter of ἄτομος (átomos, “indivisible”). For sense "individual", semantic loan from French individu. For sense in physics, semantic loan from French atome.

parole.significato: platform, dais (raised stage on which one can stand or sit in order to see everyone)
parole.testo: Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἕδρα (hédra). For sense "headquarters", a semantic loan from French siège.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἔθιμον (éthimon, “usage”) (plural ἔθιμα (éthima, “customs”)), neuter of ἔθιμος (éthimos), from ἔθος (éthos) + -ιμος (-imos), with semantic loan from French coutume.
Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἔκθεσις (ékthesis), from ἐκ (ek) + θέσις f (thésis) & semantic loan from French exposition. By surface analysis, έκ- (ék-) + θέση (thési).

parole.significato: inspiration (the act of an elevating or stimulating influence upon the intellect, emotions or creativity)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἔμπνευσις (émpneusis, “blowing in”) with semantic loan from French inspiration. By surface analysis, εμπνέω (empnéo) + -ση (-si).
From French instinct.

parole.significato: honourable (UK), honorable (US) (worthy of respect; conforming to what honour dictates)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἔντιμος (éntimos, “honoured”) with semantic loan from French honnête and honorable.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἕνω(σις) (hénō(sis)) + modern ending -ση (-si), the former a nominal formation from ενώνω (enóno, “to unite”). The modern sense of "association of companies or states" is a semantic loan from French union.
Borrowed from French extra.

parole.significato: sound coming from the nasal cavity
parole.testo: From earlier ἔνρινος (énrinos), with regressive assimilation; from Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + ῥίς (rhís, “nose”) + -ος (-os). The phonetic sense is a semantic loan from French nasal. The Hellenistic Koine noun ἔρρινον (érrhinon, “sneazing medicine”) is semantically unrelated.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἵππος (híppos, “horse”). Sense 4 is a semantic loan from French cheval.
Borrowed from French à la carte. See α λα (a la) and αλά (alá).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek αἴρω (aírō). * For sense αίρω (“remove”): Semantic loan from French lever. * For sense αίρω (“rise”): Semantic loan from French élever.

A learned creation ἀββαεῖον (avvaeíon), from ἀββ(ᾶς) (abb(âs)) + neuter suffix -εῖον (-eîon) > modern -είο (-eío), with simplification of double consonant and accents. A calque of French abbaye (“abbey”), from Latin abbatīa.
Borrowed from French avant-garde.
αβανγκάρντ (avangkárnt, “avant-garde”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), calque of French avant-gardiste.
Borrowed from French avantage.
Learned borrowing from French anglophone. By surface analysis, αγγλό- (angló-) + -φωνος (-fonos).
Borrowed from French engagé.

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἀγνώμων (agnṓmōn, “opinionless, lacking any judgement, hard-hearted,”), from Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “un-”) (α- (a-) privative) + γνώμη (gnṓmē, “opinion, counsel”). Semantic loan from French ingrat. Also substantivised. :* The ancient neuter ἄγνωμον (ágnōmon), with stress
From αγχώ(νω) (anchó(no)) + -τικός (-tikós) with semantic loan from French angoissé.
αγώγιμος (agógimos, “conductive”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity”), calque of French conductivité. First attested 1890.
Borrowed from French adénite.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀδιάθετος (adiáthetos, “not set in order, intestate (without leaving a will)”). The "ill, unwell" sense is a semantic loan from French indisposé.
Learned formation from αδιάθε(τος) (adiáthe(tos), “indisposed”) + -σία (-sía), formed as a calque of French indisposition.
Inherited from Ancient Greek ἀδικῶ (adikô), contracted form of ἀδικέω (adikéō). For the modern senses, semantic loan from French faire injustice.
Learned borrowing from French adrénaline. Suffix -ίνη (-íni, “-ine”).
From French aérobiose.
Learned borrowing from French aérodrome from ἀήρ (aḗr, “air”), αερο- (aero-) + δρόμος (drómos, “track”). Different sense of the ancient ἀεροδρόμος (aerodrómos, “traversing the air”).

parole.significato: aerosol (fine solid or liquid dispersed in a gas)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French aérosol.
Borrowed from French aéroplane; the first component of the word is ultimately from the same Greek origin as αερο- (aero-).
Borrowed from French ajour.
From French athéisme < athé(e) from Ancient Greek ἄθεος (átheos).
From French athéiste.
From French éthane (“ethane”).
From αιθύλιο (aithýlio) + -ικός (-ikós), calque of French éthylique.
French éthyle
Compound from αιμο- (aimo-, “haemo- (bloοd)”) + -ληψία (-lipsía, “taking, seizing”), a calque of French prise de sang
From French hémophilie, a French-coined term adopted into Greek, equivalent to αιμο- (aimo-, “blood, haemo-”) + -φιλία (-filía, “friend of, love of, -philia”). First attested 1887.

Learned borrowing from French acardie. See Late Latin acardia < a- privative + -cardia, formed on Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “-less”) + κᾰρδῐ́ᾱ (kărdĭ́ā, “heart”) + -ῐ́ᾱ (-ĭ́ā, suffix forming abstract nouns). Equivalent to α- (a-) + καρδ(ιά) (kard(iá)) + -ία (-ía).
Learnedly, from Hellenistic Koine Greek ἀκατάσβεστος (akatásbestos) and semantic loan from French inextinguible. From privative ἀ- (a-) + κατασβέννυμι (katasbénnumi, “extinguish completely”).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀκατάστατος (akatástatos, “unstable, irregular”), with semantic loan from French désordonné, en désordre, as well as semantic loan from German unordentlich.
From French acétone (“acetone”).
Calque of French audiomètrie. From ακοόμετρ(ο) (“audiometre”) + -ία. Morphologically, ακο(ή) (“hearing”) + -ο- + μέτρ(ο) (“-meter”) + -ία.

parole.significato: watercolour (the method, materials and end product)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French aquarelle.
Semantic loan from French acoustique, coined by Joseph Sauveur from Ancient Greek ἀκουστικός (“of or for hearing”).
Calque of French audiogramme. Morphologically from ακοή (akoḯ, “hearing”) + γράμμα (grámma, “letter”).
Calque of French audiomètre. From ακο(ή) (“hearing”) + -ο- + -μετρον > -μετρο (“-meter”).
From Ancient Greek ἀκροάζομαι (akroázomai). For auscultate, semantic loan from French ausculter.

Reborrowing from French acrobatie < acrobate, itself from Koine Greek ἀκροβάτης (akrobátēs) from ἄκρον (ákron, “peak”) -βάτης (-bátēs, “walker”) (not from ᾰ̓κρόβασις (ăkróbasis, “support e.g. foot of table”). For figurative sense, it is a calque of French faire des acrobaties.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀκρόᾱσις (akróāsis) & semantic loan from French audience and auscultation
From French activiste.

From Ancient Greek ἀκτινογραφία (aktinographía, “description of light rays”). The modern medical sense of X-ray or radiography in modern times is derived from ακτίνα (aktína, “ray, radius”) + -γραφία (-grafía, “-graphy”), calque of French radiographie. Modern medical sense first attested 1897.

parole.significato: fluoroscopy (real-time examination of the interior organs using X-rays)
parole.testo: From ακτίνα (aktína, “ray, radius”) + -σκόπηση (-skópisi, “-scopy”), calque of French radioscopie.

parole.significato: in the style of, in the manner of; à la
parole.testo: Borrowed from French à la.
Learned borrowing from French aller-retour written in Greek alphabet.
Borrowed from French algorithme.
From αλεξ- (alex-, “protection, deflection”) + ήλιος (ílios, “sun”), calque of French parasol.
From αλεξι- (alexi-, “protection, deflection”) + πτώση (ptósi, “fall”), calque of French parachute. First attested 1874.
From αλεξι- (alexi-, “protection, deflection”) + πυρ (pyr, “fire”), calque of French pare-feu. First attested 1861.
From αλεξι- (alexi-, “protection, deflection”) + βροχή (vrochí, “rain”), calque of French parapluie. Attested since 1897 in Katharevousa as ἀλεξιβρόχιον (alexivróchion).
From αλεξι- (alexi-, “protection, deflection”) + κεραυνός (keravnós, “thunderbolt”), calque of French parafoudre. First attested 1782.
αλεξίπτωτο (alexíptoto, “parachute”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), calque of French parachutiste.
Borrowed from French alcali, from Arabic اَلْقِلْي (al-qily, “alkali”).
Borrowed from French alcaloïde.
Borrowed from French alcaloïde.
Borrowed from French alcotest.
Learned borrowing from French alcool.

parole.significato: solidarity, fellowship (the mutual guarantee of support and friendship)
parole.testo: Learnedly, from Hellenistic Koine Greek ἀλληλεγγύη (allēlengúē, “mutual guarantee”) & semantic loan from French solidarité. Morphologically, αλληλ- (allil-, “mutuality: of each other”) + εγγύηση (engýisi, “guarantee”)
αλληλο- (allilo-, “reciprocal, mutual”) + βοήθεια (voḯtheia, “aid, help”), calque of French entraide.

parole.significato: almanac a diary of astronomical events.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French almanach (“calendar”), from Latin almanachus (“calendar”).
Άλπεις (Álpeis, “Alps”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), calque of French alpiniste.

parole.significato: halt, stop, don't move (order to stop moving)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French halte, from German halt. First attested 1876.
Borrowed from French alternative.
Calque of French altruiste.
αλχημεία (alchimeía, “alchemy”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), calque of French alchimiste.
Reborrowing from French amalgame, from Medieval Latin amalgama, from Arabic مَلْغَم (malḡam), from Ancient Greek μάλαγμᾰ (málagmă). Doublet of μάλαμα (málama).
Learned borrowing from French ammonite, from Άμμων (Ámmon, “Ammon”) + -ίτης (-ítis, “-ite”).

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀμνησία (amnēsía), semantic loan from French amnésie, from Ancient Greek privative ἀ- (a-) + stem μνη- of verb μιμνῄσκω (mimnēískō, “remind”) + suffix for abstract feminine nouns -σία (-sía)
From French amoraliste.
Borrowed from French amortisseur.
Borrowed from French ampère (“ampere”).
Borrowed from French abat-jour.
Borrowed from French emballage (“packaging”).
Borrowed from French emballer (“to wrap up”) via αμπαλάρω (ampaláro, “to wrap”).
Borrowed from French habillé.
Borrowed from French abonné.
Borrowed from French abri (“shelter”).
Borrowed from French embrayage (“clutch”).

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀμφίβολος (amphíbolos). For sense "questionable", semantic loan from French douteux. Morphologically, αμφι- (amfi-) + stem βολ- for which see αμφιβάλλω (amfivállo, “Ι doubt”) - αμφιβολία f (amfivolía) & βάλλω (vállo) - βολή (volí) + suffix -ος (-os).

parole.significato: to hesitate, to vacillate, to waver
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀμφιταλαντεύω (amphitalanteúō, “to balance the weight of”) with semantic loan from French vaciller. By surface analysis, αμφι- (amfi-) + ταλαντεύομαι (talantévomai).

parole.significato: host of a party or dinner, amphitryon
parole.testo: From proper noun Αμφιτρύωνας (Amfitrýonas). Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek Ἀμφιτρύων (Amphitrúōn) from the accusative singular "τόν Ἀμφιτρύωνα" from ἀμφί (amphí) & τρύω (trúō, “wear out”). Semantic loan from French amphitryon from the comedy by Molière Amphitryon, as in the verses: : le vérita
Borrowed from French amok, from Malay amuk (“to go on a killing spree”).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀνάμνησις (anámnēsis, “calling to mind, reminiscence”) + suffix -ση (-si), with semantic loan from French mémoire.
Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἀνέρχομαι (anérkhomai). By surface analysis, αν- (an-, “up”, from ανα- (ana-)) + έρχομαι (érchomai, “come”). For sense amount: semantic loan from French s'élever.
Learnedly, from Ancient Greek ἀνία (anía) & Semantic loan from French ennui.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀναγνωρίζω (anagnōrízō). From the sense "admit" Semantic loan from French reconnaître. Morphologically, from ανα- (ana-, “repeated”) + γνωρίζω (gnorízo, “know”).
From Koine Greek ἀναζωογονῶ. Semantic loan from French ranimer. Morphologically analysed as ανα- (ana-, “re-”) + ζωογονώ (zoogonó, “give life, vitalise”).
Calque of French réanimation. Morphologically, from αναζωογονη- (“stem from αναζωογονώ, revitilise”) + -ση (“from suffix -σις”)

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀναιμίᾱ (anaimíā) from ἄναιμος (ánaimos, “bloddless”) and semantic loan from French anémie from Ancient Greek ἀναιμίᾱ (anaimíā). By surface analysis, αν- (an-, α- privative) + Ancient Greek αἷμα (haîma).
Learnedly from ανακριβής (anakrivís) + -εια (-eia), a calque of French inexactitude.
From Ancient Greek ἀναλύω (“unloose; resolve into its elements”). For modern senses, semantic loan from French analyser and English analyse. Morphologically, from ανα- + λύω.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀναμένω (anaménō, “to wait”), from ἀνα- (ana-) + μένω (ménō), with semantic loan from French s'attendre and Semantic loan from English is expected.
From αναξιοπρεπ(ής) (anaxioprep(ís)) + -εια (-eia), a calque of French indignité. Alternatively, from αν- (an-, α- privative) + αξιοπρέπεια (axioprépeia, “dignity”).
Calque of French reproduire. Morphologically ανα- (ana-) + παράγω (parágo).
Calque of French représenter, from ανα- (ana-) + παριστάνω (paristáno). Ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀνα- (ana-) + παρα- (para-) + ἵστημι (hístēmi).
Calque of French nouvelle enchère. Morphologically, from ανα- (“again”) + πλειστηριασμός (“auction”).
Learnedly from αναπληρώ(νω) (anapliró(no)) + -τής (-tís), a calque of French suppléant.
Learnedly from αν- (an-, α- privative) + αποτελεσματικός (apotelesmatikós), a calque of French ineffectif (rare) and English ineffective.
From αν- (an-, α- privative) + αποφάσισα (apofásisa, “decide”) + -τος (-tos), a calque of French indécis. First attested 1888.
αναποφάσιστος (anapofásistos, “undecided, undecisive”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity, -ness”), calque of French indécision. First attested 1877.
From French anarchisme (“anarchism”).
Learnedly from ανασκοπώ (anaskopó) + -ση (-si), a calque of French révision and English review.
Learnedly from ανα- (ana-) + συνθέτω (synthéto), a calque of French recomposer.
ανα- (“re-”) + συνιστώ (“establish”) from the ancient verb συνιστῶ (sunistô), συνίστημι (sunístēmi). Calque of French reconstituer. First attested in 1833.
Learnedly from ανασυνθέ(τω) (anasynthé(to)) + -ση (-si), a calque of French recomposition.
Learnedly from ανασυστή(νω) (anasystí(no)) + -ση (-si), a calque of French reconstitution.

parole.significato: to spring up, arise (e.g. of problems, new issues)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓νᾰφῠ́ομαι (ănăphŭ́omai, “I am grown again”) of active ᾰ̓νᾰφῠ́ω. The figurative sense, a semantic loan from French surgir. Morphologically, from ανα- (“again”) + φύομαι (fýomai, “grow”).
From Ancient Greek ἀναχώρησις (anakhṓrēsis, “retreat, return”) + -ση (-sē). For the modern meaning of "departure", semantic loan from French depart.
Learned formation from the nominalized neuter of αναψυκτικός (anapsyktikós, “soft drink”), with semantic loan from French rafraîchissement.
Learned formation from αναψυκ- (anapsyk-), combining form of αναψύχω (anapsýcho, “to cool down”), + -τικός (-tikós), with semantic loan from French rafraîchissant.
From French androgène.
From αν- (an-, α- privative) + εκτιμώ (ektimó) + -τος (-tos). Calque of French inestimable, inappréciable.
From ανεμισ- (anemis-), the past stem of ανεμίζω (anemízo, “to air, ventilate”), + -τήρας (-tíras) (< -τήρ (-tḗr)); calque of French ventilateur.
From αν- (an-, α- privative) + εξαρτώ (exartó, “depend upon or owe [one’s] existence to”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix), calque of French indépendant. First attested 1829.
Learnedly from αν- (an-, “re-”, from ανα- (ana-)) + εφοδιάζω (efodiázo, “supply”), a calque of French approvisionner.

parole.significato: worrying, concerning, disquieting, troubling, alarming, disturbing (causing worry, anxiety)
parole.testo: Learnedly from the ανησυχη- stem of ανησυχώ (anisychó) + -τικός (-tikós), a calque of French inquiétant.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀνθηρός (anthērós) - see ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”). For the figurative sense, semantic loan from French florissant.
Learnedly from άνθρακ(ας) (ánthrak(as)) + -ούχος (-oúchos), a calque of French carbonifère and German kohlehaltig.
From Ancient Greek ἀνομοίωσις (anomoíōsis). Semantic loan from French dissimilation.
From French entente.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ᾰ̓ντᾰλλᾰγή (ăntăllăgḗ) with semantic loan from French échange. By surface analysis, αντ- (ant-) + αλλαγή (allagí).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀντιδρῶ (antidrô, “to act in return”), with semantic loan from French réagir. By surface analysis, αντι- (anti-) + δρω (dro).
Unadapted borrowing from French antiquaire.

parole.significato: cash on delivery used in the phrases
parole.testo: αντικαταβάλλω (antikatavállo) + -η (-i), from Ancient Greek ἀντικαταβάλλω (antikatabállō), from ἀντι- (anti-) + καταβάλλω (katabállō). For the modern sense of "cash on delivery", calque of French contre remboursement.
Learnedly from αντι- (anti-) + κατοπτρίζω (katoptrízo) with semantic loan from French refléter in the figurative sense.
αντικειμενικός (antikeimenikós, “objective”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity, -ness”), calque of French objectivité. First attested 1867.
Borrowed from French antiquaire + -ερί (-erí, suffix for shops).
αντι- (anti-) + κλέπτ(ης) (klépt(is)) (κλέφτης (kléftis)) + -ικός (-ikós). Calque of French antivol.
A learned αντιδάνειο (antidáneio, “repatriated loanword”): From French antilope (“antelope”), from Medieval Latin antilops, from Byzantine Greek ἀνθόλοψ (anthólops).

parole.significato: disagreeable, dislikable, unlikable, unpleasant (of person, personality, etc.)
parole.testo: Learnedly from the αντιπαθη- stem of αντιπαθώ (antipathó) + -τικός (-tikós), with semantic loan from French antipathique. Compare Koine Greek ἀντιπαθητικός (antipathētikós, “opposed to passivity”).
Learnedly from αντι- (anti-) + πειθαρχικός (peitharchikós). Calque of French insubordonné.
From French antiseptique.
Borrowed from French entrée.
From French enfant gâté (spoilt/spoiled child).
From αν- (an-, α- privative) + ωριμότητα (orimótita, “maturity, ripeness”); a calque of French immaturité.
ανώτερος (anóteros, “higher, superior”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity, -ness”), calque of French supériorité. First attested 1886.
Calque of French Société Anonyme.

parole.significato: unripe, immature (not ready for reaping or gathering)
parole.testo: From αν- (an-, α- privative) + ώριμος (órimos, “mature, ripe”); calque of French immature.
From French accessoire.
Learned borrowing from French axiologique. By surface analysis, αξιολογ(ία) (axiolog(ía)) + -ικός (-ikós).
Learnedly from αξιο- (axio-) + -ποιώ (-poió), a calque of French mettre en valeur.
From αξιο- (axio-, “worthy, deserving”) + σημειώνω (simeióno, “to note”). Calque of French notable attested in 1808.

parole.significato: depreciation (the state of being depreciated; disparagement)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἀπαξίωσις (apaxíōsis) with semantic loan from French dépréciation (in the economic sense). By surface analysis, απαξιώ(νω) (apaxió(no)) + -ση (-si).
From Ancient Greek ἀπαραίτητος (aparaítētos, “inexorable; not to be moved by prayer”), with semantic loan from French inévitable, indispensable.

parole.significato: to set free, to liberate, to emancipate
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀπελευθερῶ (apeleutherô), contracted form of ἀπελευθερόω (apeleutheróō, “to emancipate (a slave), to manumit”), with semantic loan from French libérer. By surface analysis, απ- (ap-) + ελευθερώνω (eleftheróno) or απελεύθερος (apeléftheros) + -ώνω (-óno).
From French apéritif.

Perfect participle of αποστέλλομαι (apostéllomai), passive voice of αποστέλλω (“send, dispatch”). Learnedly, from Hellenistic Koine Greek ἀπεσταλμένος (apestalménos), participle of the ancient verb ἀποστέλλω (apostéllō) & semantic loan from French envoyé. Also substantivised.

parole.significato: to address, to deliver (a written or oral communication to)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀπευθύνω (apeuthúnō, “to direct”) with semantic loan from French (s')adresser.
From French applique (“wall light”), from Latin applicare (“to attach”).
Borrowed from French haplologie (“haplology”), from Ancient Greek ἁπλόος (haplóos, “simple”) + -λογία (-logía, “knowledge”).
From απλοποιώ (aplopoió) + -ση (-si), a calque of French simplification. Also analyzable as απλ(ός) (apl(ós)) + -ο- (-o-) + -ποίηση (-poíisi).
απο- (apo-, “negation”) + γοητεύω (goïtévo, “to charm, to enthrall”). Calque of French désenchanter.
Learnedly from απο- (apo-) + δεσμεύω (desmévo), a calque of French dégager, désengager and German entbinden. Compare Ancient Greek ἀποδεσμεύω (apodesmeúō, “to bind fast”).
From αποδόμη- (apodómi-, stem of αποδομώ (apodomó)) + -ση (-si) or απο- (apo-) + δόμηση (dómisi). In the 'deconstruction' senses, a calque of French déconstruction.

parole.significato: to discourage, to dishearten, to dispirit, to daunt

Learnedly, from Hellenistic Koine Greek ἀποκεφαλίζω. The figurative sense, semantic loan from French décapiter. Morphologically, from απο- (apo-, “de”) + κεφάλι (kefáli, “head”) + -ίζω (-ízo, suffix for verbs).

parole.significato: indisputably, unarguably, undeniably, without discussion or argument

parole.significato: elusive, at large, unapprehended, uncaught, not arrested

parole.significato: self-examination; self-exam (the act of checking one's own body for abnormalities by feeling or pressing with the hands…

parole.significato: narrative (the systematic recitation of an event or series of events)

From Ancient Greek ἀφομοίωσις (aphomoíōsis). Semantic loan from French assimilation.

parole.significato: switch (device to isolate an electric current)

parole.significato: decoration, ornamentation (the act of adorning or embellishing)

parole.significato: diachronic (of, pertaining to or concerned with changes that occur over time)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French diachronique. By surface analysis, διαχρον(ία) (diachron(ía)) + -ικός (-ikós).

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek διεγείρω (diegeírō, “wake up; raise”) from δια- (dia-) and ἐγείρω (egeírō, “raise”). By surface analysis, δι- (δια-) + εγείρω (egeíro, “raise”). For psychological and sexual senses, semantic loan from French exciter.
From δι- from δια- (di- from dia-) + έθν(ος) (éthn(os), “nation”) + -ής (-ís). Calque of French international.
διεθνής (“international”) + -ισμός * (as theory): Calque of French internationalisme. Attested since 1893. * (linguistics): Calque of German Internationalismus.
From Koine Greek διευθύνω (dieuthúnō, “to make straight, to rule”). For the modern sense of "to direct, manage", semantic loan from French diriger.
Learnedly from δι(α)- (di(a)-) + ευκολύνω (efkolýno) with semantic loan from French faciliter.

Perfect participle of διαφθείρομαι (diaftheíromai), passive voice of διαφθείρω (diaftheíro). Learnedly, from Ancient Greek διεφθαρμένος (diephtharménos, “destroyed”) & semantic loan from French corrompu. Morphologically, from δι- (δια-) (di- (dia-)) + the ancient participle ἐφθαρμένος (ephtharménos)
From Ancient Greek δικαίωμα (dikaíōma), by surface analysis, δίκαιος (díkaios, “just”) + -ωμα (-oma). In parts a semantic loan from French droit .

parole.significato: to justify (to provide an acceptable explanation for)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek δικαιολογῶ (dikaiologô), from Ancient Greek δικαιολογέομαι (dikaiologéomai, “plead one's cause before the judge”), with semantic loan from French justifier.

parole.significato: diplomacy (the art and practice of conducting international relations)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French diplomatie with -ία (-ía) suffix.

Learnedly from δυσ- (dys-) + ανάλογος (análogos), a calque of French disproportionné.
Calque of French dysménorrhée. First attested in 1876.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek δῠτικός (dŭtikós). Morphologically δύω (dýo) + -τικός (-tikós). In the proper senses, semantic loan from French occidental and English western.
Inherited from Ancient Greek δύναμις (dúnamis). For scientific and modern senses, semantic loan from French puissance or English power.

parole.significato: collection, receipt (of payments due, taxes, etc.)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek εἴσπραξις (eíspraxis) with semantic loan from French perception. By surface analysis, εισπρά(ττω) (eisprá(tto)) + -ξη (-xi).
Borrowed from French évaporé.

From Koine Greek εγγύη(σις) (engúē(sis)) + -ση (-si), from the Ancient Greek ἐγγύη (engúē). For modern senses, a semantic loan from French garantie and English guaranty.

parole.significato: to establish, put into effect, set up
parole.testo: Semantic loan from French ériger from Ancient Greek ἐγκᾰθιδρῡ́ω (“erect, set up in”). Morphologically, from εν- (εγ-) (“in-”) + κατα- (-καθ-) (“fully”) + ιδρύω (“found”).
Perfect participle of εγκαθίσταμαι (egkathístamai), passive voice of εγκαθιστώ (“install, reside”), a calque of French établi or installé.
Learned borrowing from French encyclopédique. By surface analysis, εγκυκλοπαίδ(εια) (egkyklopaíd(eia)) + -ικός (-ikós).

parole.significato: to be pregnant (with), to carry (to have developing offspring within one's body)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐγκυμονῶ (enkumonô), from Ancient Greek ἐγκυμονέω (enkumonéō), with semantic loan from French être gros de in the figurative sense.

parole.significato: circular (official directive or notice intended for circulation)
parole.testo: Learned nominalization of the feminine form of the adjective εγκύκλιος, with semantic loan from French circulaire.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐγρήγορσις (egrḗgorsis) with -ση (-si) ending and semantic loan from French vigilance.
Borrowed from French égoïsme. By surface analysis, εγώ (egó) + -ισμός (-ismós).
Borrowed from French égoïste. By surface analysis, εγωισμός (egoïsmós) + -ιστής (-istís).
Borrowed from French égoïstique. By surface analysis, εγωιστής (egoïstís) + -ικός (-ikós).
εθνικός (ethnikós, “national”) + -ότητα (-ótita, “-ity”), calque of French nationalité. First attested 1833.

parole.significato: to specialize (to train (someone) in a speciality)
parole.testo: Learnedly from ειδικ(ός) (eidik(ós)) + -εύω (-évo), a calque of French spécialiser.

parole.significato: speciality (UK), specialty (US), specialism (that in which one specializes; a chosen expertise or talent)
parole.testo: Learnedly from ειδικ(ός) (eidik(ós)) + -ότητα (-ótita), a calque of French specialité.

parole.significato: in ancient Greek and Roman literature, a short bucolic poem, usually with romantic theme
parole.testo: The genre from Hellenistic Ancient Greek εἰδύλλιον (eidúllion, “short bucolic poem”). Sense romance, semantic loan from French idylle.
Learnedly from εικονογραφ(ία) (eikonograf(ía), “iconography”) + -ικός (-ikós) with semantic loan from French pictographique.

parole.significato: iconolatry (the use of images as symbols that provide an inspiration and aid to worship, especially in the context of t…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French iconolâtrie, from Byzantine Greek εικονολάτρης (eikonolátrēs) + -ία (-ía).
From εικοσι- (eikosi-) + τετρα- (tetra-) + ώρ(α) (ór(a)) + -ος (-os), a calque of French vingt-quatre heures.

parole.significato: taken (emphatically e.g. of decisions, commitments, obligations), undertaken
parole.testo: Formal perfect participle of λαμβάνομαι (lamvánomai), passive voice of λαμβάνω (lamváno). In the fashion of the Hellenistic Koine Greek εἰλημμένος (eilēmménos, “who has been admitted”), participle of the ancient λαμβάνω (lambánō). parole.significato: import (something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek εἰσᾰγωγή (eisăgōgḗ) with semantic loan from French introduction.

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek εἰσπράκτωρ (eispráktōr, “tax collector”) with the accusative case ending -ορα (-ora), from εἰσ- (eis-) + πράκτωρ (práktōr), with semantic loan from French percepteur.

parole.significato: closely, at close quarters, up close
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek σύνεγγυς (súnengus, “very close”), with semantic loan from French de près.
French hectolitre, as if εκατό- (ekató-) + λίτρο (lítro)

parole.significato: manifestation (the act or process of becoming manifest)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εκδηλώνω (ekdilóno) + -ση (-si) with semantic loan from French manifestation in the sense 'event'.

parole.significato: to manifest, to show, to express (:emotion, intention, interest, etc.)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐκδηλῶ (ekdēlô, “show clearly”) with -ώνω (-óno) ending and semantic loan from French (se) manifester. By surface analysis, εκ- (ek-) + δηλώνω (dilóno).

Learnedly from unattested stem *εκκωφαν- + -τικός (-tikós), a calque of French assourdissant. The stem is formed from Ancient Greek εκ- (ek-) + κωφαίνω (kōphaínō) as a calque of Modern Greek ξεκουφαίνω (xekoufaíno).

parole.significato: éclair (small chocolate covered creme-filled pastry puff in a general oblong shape)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French éclair.
From French éclampsie.
Learned formation from the perfect participle of εκλεπτύνω (ekleptýno, “to refine”), formed as a calque of French raffiné and calque of English refined.
Learnedly from εκλογ(ή) (eklog(í)) + -ικός (-ikós), a calque of French électoral.

parole.significato: to exploit, take advantage of (wealth, resources, etc)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐκμεταλλεύω (ekmetalleúō, “to empty (a mine) of ore”), made deponent by analogy with εργάζομαι (ergázomai), and with semantic loan from French exploiter (une mine).
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐκνευρίζω (ekneurízō, “to cut the tendons”) with semantic loan from French (s')énerver. By surface analysis, εκ- (ek-) + νεύρ(ο) (névr(o)) + -ίζω (-ízo).

parole.significato: defenestration (act of throwing a person out of a window)
parole.testo: From εκ (ek, “out of, de-”) + παράθυρο (paráthyro, “window”) + -ωση (-osi, “-ation”). Calque of French défenestration.

parole.significato: to represent (to stand or act in the place of; to perform the duties, exercise the rights, or otherwise act on behalf o…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Byzantine Greek εκπροσωπώ (ekprosōpṓ), with semantic loan from French représenter. By surface analysis, εκ- (ek-) + πρόσωπο (prósopo) + -ώ (-ó).

parole.significato: execution, completion (carrying out of an order or an action)
parole.testo: From εκτελώ (ekteló, “to execute”), calque of French exécution. First attested 1840.

parole.significato: executor (person who carries out some task)
parole.testo: From εκτελώ (ekteló, “to execute”), calque of French exécutrice. First attested 1892.

parole.significato: executor (person who carries out some task)
parole.testo: From εκτελώ (ekteló), calque of French exécuteur. First attested 1812.

parole.significato: executive (concerned with the carrying out of an order or an action)
parole.testo: From εκτελώ (ekteló, “to execute”), calque of French exécutif. First attested 1796.

parole.significato: to carry out, execute, do (put into effect)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐκτελέω (ekteléō, “complete, bring to an end”), from ἐκ- (ek-, “from, out of”) + τέλος (télos, “completion, end”) and a semantic loan from French exécuter. Sense "perform" developed in Medieval Greek.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐκτροπή (ektropḗ) with semantic loan from French déviation.

parole.significato: oil painting (a painting in oil paints, or the technique or process)
parole.testo: From ελαιο (elaio, “oil”) + γραφία (grafía, “painting”) a calque of French peinture a l'huile.
Learned borrowing from French hélicoptère, itself coined from Ancient Greek elements. By surface analysis, έλικας (élikas, “propeller, helix”) + φτερό (fteró, “wing”).

parole.significato: elliptical, elliptic (in a shape of, or reminding of, an ellipse; oval)
parole.testo: In the geometry sense, a learned borrowing from French elliptique, from New Latin ellipticus, from Koine Greek ἐλλειπτικός (elleiptikós). In the grammar/linguistic senses, a learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐλλειπτικός (elleiptikós).

parole.significato: enamel, enamelled ware (vitreous coating especially cobalt blue, mainly household wares, often decorative)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French émaillé (“enamelled”).

parole.significato: embolism (an obstruction or occlusion of a blood vessel by an embolus)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐμβολή (embolḗ) with semantic loan from French embolie, borrowed from the same etymon.

parole.significato: deciding or acting based on one's experience, not theoretical knowledge (sometimes derogatory)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French empirisme.
Learnedly from εμ- (em-) + πλούτ(ος) (ploút(os)) + -ίζω (-ízo), a calque of French enrichir.
Perfect participle of εμπνέομαι (empnéomai), passive voice of εμπνέω (“inspire”) from Ancient Greek ἐμπνέω (“breathe upon; inspire”). The modern sense, calque of French inspiré.
εν (en, “in”) + φιάλη (fiáli, “bottle”) + -ώνω (-óno, “verb ending”), calque of French embouteiller. First attested 1892.

parole.significato: in any case, at any rate, anyhow, regardless
parole.testo: A calque of French en tout cas. Katharevousa set phrase (polytonic spelling: ἐν πάσῃ περιπτώσει) with preposition ἐν (en, “in”), the feminine singular dative πάσῃ (pásēi) of πᾶς (pâs, “everyone”) & περίπτωσις (períptōsis, “encountering”) -modern περίπτωση (períptosi, “case, instance”)-.
From Hellenistic Koine Greek ἐν ὄψει (en ópsei): preposition ἐν (en) & singular dative of feminine noun ὄψις (ópsis). For the preposition, semantic loan from French en vue de.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐνήλικος (enḗlikos) with semantic loan from French adulte.

parole.significato: aware, informed, cognizant, up-to-date, abreast of
parole.testo: εν- (en-, “in-”) + ημέρα (iméra, “day”) + -ος (-os, “adjectival suffix”), i.e. "aware of the day's events", formed as a calque of French à jour (“up to date”) based on the model of older terms such as ἐφήμερος (ephḗmeros, “short-lived”). Attested since 1871.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐναλλαγή (enallagḗ, “exchange; variety”), with semantic loan from French alternance and alternation.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐναλλακτικός (enallaktikós, “altered”), with semantic loan from French alternatif and English alternative.

parole.significato: active (having the power or quality of acting)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐνεργητικός (energētikós) with semantic loan from French actif in the accounting sense. By surface analysis, ενεργώ (energó) + -τικός (-tikós).

parole.significato: orchestration (arrangement of music for performance by an orchestra)
parole.testo: εν- (en-) + ορχήστρα (orchístra, “orchestra”), calque of French orchestration. First attested 1889.

parole.significato: to orchestrate (arrange music for performance by an orchestra)
parole.testo: ορχήστρ(α) (orchístr(a), “in”) + ορχήστρα (orchístra, “orchestra”) + -ώνω (-óno, suffix for verbs), calque of French orchestrer.

parole.significato: to pour liquid drop by drop
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἐνσταλάζω. For sense instil, semantic loan from French instiller. Also see σταλάσσω (stalássō) and στάζω (stázō). Morphologically, from εν- (“in”) + σταλάζω (“drip”).

parole.significato: to locate, to pinpoint (to find out where something is located)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εν- (en-) + τόπ(ος) (tóp(os)) + -ίζω (-ízo), with semantic loan from French localiser.
Learnedly from εν- (en-) + Ancient Greek ὑδατ(ῶ) (hudat(ô), “to be wet, watery”) + -ώνω (-óno), a calque of French hydrater.
Learned univerbation of εξ (ex) + άλλου (állou), a calque of French d'autre part.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐξαίρεσῐς (exaíresĭs) with -ση (-si) ending and semantic loan from French exception.

parole.significato: to purify (to free from guilt or sin)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εξ- (ex-) + αγν(ός) (agn(ós), “pure”) + -ίζω (-ízo), a loose calque of French purifier.

parole.significato: excellent, fine, first-class; exceptional, unusual, great
parole.testo: From Byzantine Greek ἐξαιρετικός (exairetikós); by surface analysis, εξαίρετος (exaíretos) + -ικός (-ikós). In the modern sense of "excellent, exceptional", with semantic loan from French exceptionnel.

parole.significato: because of, on account of (implies something negative)
parole.testo: Univerbation of εξ (ex, “from, of, by”) + αιτίας (aitías, “cause”). Calque of French à cause de.

parole.significato: to exhaust, to deplete, to use up (to expend wholly, or until the supply comes to an end)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐξαντλῶ (exantlô), from Ancient Greek ἐξαντλέω (exantléō, “empty out, endure to the end”), with semantic loan from French (s')épuiser. By surface analysis, εξ- (ex-) + αντλώ (antló).

parole.significato: to train (to teach and form someone by practice)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐξασκῶ (exaskô, “to exercise fully”) with semantic loan from French exercer. By surface analysis, εξ- (ex-) + ασκώ (askó).

parole.significato: to individualize, to personalize (to modify something to suit an individual)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εξ- (ex-) + ατομικ(ός) (atomik(ós)) + -εύω (-évo), a calque of French individualiser.

parole.significato: elaborate, exquisite, recherché, sophisticated (characterized by careful, studied avoidance of the simple or ordinary)
parole.testo: Learnedly from the passive perfect participle of Koine Greek ἐκζητῶ (ekzētô), contracted form of ἐκζητέω (ekzētéō), in accordance with the meaning of the adverb ἐξεζητημένως (exezētēménōs, “exquisitely”), with semantic loan from French recherché.
Learnedly from εξ- (ex-) + ειδικ(ός) (eidik(ós)) + -εύω (-évo), a calque of French spécialiser.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐξοικειῶ (exoikeiô, “to appropriate”) with -ώνω (-óno) suffix and semantic loan from French familiariser.

parole.significato: to neutralize (to make even, inactive or ineffective)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εξ- (ex-) + ουδέτερ(ος) (oudéter(os), “neutral”) + -ώνω (-óno), a calque of French neutraliser.
Learnedly from εξουσί(α) (exousí(a)) + -ο- (-o-) + -δοτώ (-dotó), a loose calque of French autoriser.
Borrowed from French express, from English express, from French exprès.

parole.significato: born out of wedlock, illegitimate (born to unmarried parents)
parole.testo: Learnedly from εξω- (exo-) + γάμ(ος) (gám(os), “marriage”) + -ος (-os), a calque of French extraconjugal. A false friend of English exogamous.

parole.significato: to be imminent, to be about to happen, to be on the way
parole.testo: Learnedly, from the 3rd singular person ἐπίκειται (epíkeitai) of Ancient Greek ἐπίκειμαι (epíkeimai, “I am laid upon; I am urgent”) -ἐπί (epí) + κεῖμαι (keîmai)-, semantic loan from French est imminent. Morphologically analysed as επι- (epi-, “upon”) + κείμαι (keímai, “lie”).

parole.significato: furnishing (the act of providing with furniture)
parole.testo: Learnedly from επιπλώ(νω) (epipló(no), “to furnish”) + -ση (-si). Calque of French ameublement.

parole.significato: reset, resetting, restoration, return (the act or process of bringing back to a previous state)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπαναφορά (epanaphorá) (from Koine Greek in the rhetorical sense) and with semantic loan from French revenu (“tempering”).

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιβαρύνω (epibarúnō, “to press heavily on”) with semantic loan from French aggraver and German belasten. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + βαρύνω (varýno).

parole.significato: to survive, to continue to live or exist
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek *ἐπιβι(ῶ) + -ώνω (-óno), the former, of -όω (-óō) conjugation, attested in the aorist form ἐπεβίων (epebíōn, “I continued to live”) of *ἐπιβιόω "to live over", from ἐπι- (epi-) + βιόω (bióō), with semantic loan from French survivre and English survive.

parole.significato: to slow, to slow down, to decelerate (to reduce the speed of)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐπιβραδύνω (epibradúnō, “to relax”) with semantic loan from French ralentir.
From επίδειξη (epídeixi, “showing off, exhibiting”) + -ας (-as, “-er”), semantic loan from French exhibitionniste.

parole.significato: exhibitionism (practice or character trait of deliberately drawing attention to oneself)
parole.testo: From επίδειξη (epídeixi, “showing off, exhibiting”) + μανία (manía, “mania”), calque of French exhibitionnisme. First attested 1894.

parole.significato: to pursue, to seek, to be after (to try to acquire or gain; to strive after; to aim at)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιδιώκω (epidiṓkō) with semantic loan from French poursuivre. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + διώκω (dióko).

parole.significato: to survive (to live past a life-threatening event)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιζῶ (epizô), contracted form of ἐπιζώω (epizṓō), ἐπιζάω (epizáō, “to survive”), with semantic loan from French survivre and English survive. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + ζω (zo).

parole.significato: inspector (a person employed to inspect something)
parole.testo: Learnedly from επιθεωρώ (epitheoró) + -τής (-tís), with semantic loan from French inspecteur.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιθεωρῶ (epitheōrô) with semantic loan from French inspecter. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + θεωρώ (theoró).
Univerbation of επί (epí) + κεφαλής (kefalís), a learned calque of French en tête.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιπλοκή (epiplokḗ, “plaiting together; confusion”) with semantic loan from French complications.

parole.significato: influence (the power to affect, control or manipulate something or someone)

parole.significato: wavy, undulating, rippling (rising or swelling in waves)
parole.testo: Learnedly from κυματίζω (kymatízo) + -τός (-tós), a loose calque of French ondulé.

parole.significato: dominant (predominant, common, prevalent, of greatest importance)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek with semantic loan from French souverain.

parole.significato: to dominate (to govern, rule or control by superior authority or power)

parole.significato: ownership, possession (the state of having complete legal control of something)

parole.significato: comic opera, play usually including songs, musical theatre

parole.significato: cluster of flowers with a flat or convex top
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French corymbe, from Latin corymbus, from Ancient Greek κόρυμβος (kórumbos).

parole.significato: mister (title conferred on an adult male)

Learnedly from λογο- (logo-) + Ancient Greek παίγνιον (paígnion), a calque of French jeu de mots.
Learned borrowing from French luxe (pronounced as Latin lux), from Latin luxus

parole.significato: because of, due to, owing to, on account of (as a consequence of)

parole.significato: mass (quantity of matter cohering together to make one body)
parole.testo: The form of the word continues Ancient Greek μᾶζα (mâza, “barley cake”), but the sense "mass" of the modern Greek word is semantic loan from French masse (18th century), derived from Latin massa (English mass, German Masse, etc.)
Borrowed from French masque or Italian masca.

parole.significato: harridan, shrew, termagant (vicious, ill-tempered, spiteful woman)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek Μέγαιρα (Mégaira) with semantic loan from French mégère, from Latin Megaera, from Ancient Greek Μέγαιρα (Mégaira).

parole.significato: A swimsuit, a swimming costume, swimming trunks.

parole.significato: to cancel (to invalidate or annul: planned activity)
parole.testo: Learnedly from Ancient Greek ματαιῶ (mataiô, “to bring to naught”) + -ώνω (-óno), with semantic loan from French rendre vain.

parole.significato: blackboard (black board that can be written upon with chalk)
parole.testo: μαυρο- (mavro-, “black”) + πίνακας (pínakas, “board, sign”), calque of French tableau noir. First attested 1838.

parole.significato: mahogany (red-brown wood of the tree genus Swietenia)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French mahagoni.

parole.significato: minority group, minority (a group that forms only a small part of the population, whether it be for ethnic or other rea…

parole.significato: minority (any subgroup that does not form a numerical majority)
parole.testo: Learnedly from μειο- (meio-) + ψήφ(ος) (psíf(os)) + -ία (-ía), modelled on πλειοψηφία (pleiopsifía). A calque of French minorité.

μετασχηματ- (metaschimat-, “to transform”) + -ιστής (-istís, “-ist, -er”), calque of French transformateur.

parole.significato: metronome (device used to mark time-tempo by means of regular ticks)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French métronome, from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron, “measure”) + νόμος (nómos, “regulation, law”).

parole.significato: group, bunch, gang (of people or friends)

parole.significato: visibility (the degree to which things may be seen)

parole.significato: to egg on, to encourage, to urge

Borrowed from French paraphonie, from Ancient Greek πᾰρᾰ́φρων (părắphrōn).

parole.significato: to grant, to concede (to give, confer, make concession of: land, place, right, etc.)

parole.significato: to attend, to be in attendance (to be present at an event)

parole.significato: denominator, the lower part of a fraction (thus 2 in ½).

parole.significato: digestive, peptic (of, relating to, or functioning in digestion)
